findings.title: Exit code 4 changes meaning from recreate-required to feature-disabled
findings.body: This PR changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. Exit code 4 was the actual value emitted by the previous implementation, so any existing automation that used the real binary contract (rather than the older documentation) will now interpret a disabled-preview-feature result as “recreate upgrade required” and may proceed to shut down the deployment instead of treating the command as unavailable. Since the documentation explicitly calls the exit code the stable scripting interface, avoid reusing the existing numeric code for a new condition or ensure all consumers are updated in the same change.

findings.title: Documented exit codes are not asserted in the CLI tests
findings.body: The new feature-disabled test only asserts the error text, not that the command exits with the newly documented code 4. Likewise, `testWrongVersions` only checks the incompatibility message and does not assert that an incompatible result exits with the newly documented code 3. Since the PR changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`, a regression in the exit-code contract would pass these tests even though automation relies on those codes. Add `assertEquals(4, result.exitCode())` for the disabled-feature case and `assertEquals(3, result.exitCode())` for the incompatible-version cases, covering both `metadata` and `check` subcommands where applicable.
